simple: One of the big things this university prepares you to build, such as an operating system, GPU kernels, a robot or a drone.
analogy: One trade on a building site: heating, electrics, plumbing.
precise: In the MP8 card, the areas a proposal must combine (at least two); in the MP8 handbook an area counts when the learner brings a finished mega project of it (MP1–MP7) whose acceptance tests still pass from a clean checkout. The counting rule is the handbook's proposal.
source: D1 of MP8 (guide 11.6, MP8 card; pending owner confirmation of the counting rule)

simple: A slower, simpler implementation that keeps exactly the same promise as the real one, so the rest of the system can be built and tested before the real one runs.
analogy: A temporary electric heater in the finished room, wired to the same thermostat line the real boiler will use.
precise: An implementation of a component behind an interface contract that produces contract-conforming outputs with identical semantics without the target hardware (in MP8's lab, the CPU loop running the same per-cell rule as the GPU kernel); it is the stub of the walking skeleton and remains as a test reference after the real backend arrives. Course definition.
source: course definition, MP8 (lab run R1 of MP8)

simple: A table of the things you will break on purpose, and what the system must do each time.
analogy: The list of drills: power cut, burst pipe, smoke in the kitchen, each with the right reaction.
precise: A list of injected faults at each interface or component, each with the expected observable behaviour, the acceptance test that checks it and its result; generalises the failover matrix of F12-28 and MP7's failsafe matrix to an integrated system. Course definition.

simple: The list of what could still go wrong with the project, who watches each risk, and which milestone removes it.
analogy: The site manager's list: the roof tiles may arrive late; the ground may be soft.
precise: A table kept in the project repository with, per risk, a description, likelihood and impact (judgements), owner, the milestone or spike that retires it and its current state; reviewed at every design-review gate. Introduced in F12-28, named in MP8. Course definition.

simple: The features you agree in advance to drop first if time runs out.
analogy: If we are late, the garden path waits; the roof does not.
precise: An ordered list in a mega-project proposal of features (never tests) that may be removed with the reviewers' agreement at a gate; scope is the only variable a late project may cut, because acceptance tests are never skipped or weakened without approval and a log entry (curriculum sections 0 and 19.2).
source: D2 of MP8 (curriculum 0, 19.2; pending verification); course definition
